questions.prompt: What kind of framework is Pipecat?
questions.answer: An open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and multimodal conversational agents.
questions.sourceQuote: open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and multimodal conversational agents

questions.prompt: What command does the README suggest to dive right in?
In Pipecat's multi-agent model, what is each pipeline?
questions.answer: Each pipeline is an agent, and agents can be composed with handoff, parallel fan-out, sidecar workers or distributed deployments.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that Pipecat is pluggable?
questions.answer: It supports many AI services and tools.
questions.sourceQuote: Supports many AI services and tools

questions.prompt: What is Pipecat Flows used for?
questions.answer: Predefined or dynamic conversation paths with state management.
questions.sourceQuote: predefined or dynamic conversation paths with state management

questions.prompt: Which tool must be installed first to run Pipecat locally?
Why does a manual installation add extras such as pipecat-ai[option,...]?
questions.answer: Only the core framework is included by default to keep things lightweight; extras add third-party AI services.
questions.sourceQuote: only the core framework is included by default

questions.prompt: What is the minimum Python version for developing Pipecat?
How do you run all of Pipecat's tests?
questions.answer: uv run pytest from the root directory.
